title.narrative: The NCD management course provided for 200 chronic NCD patients annually

# of chronic NCD patients, disaggregated by age, gender, nationality, vulnerability, and Caritas health clinic have been enrolled in and completed a comprehensive NCD management course At least 75% of chronic NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course have adopted and are applying healthier dietary and lifestyle changes for improved self-monitoring and daily management of their disease40% of the most vulnerable NCD patients have received regular prescribed NCD medication support

target.value: 114 NCD patients enrolled in and completed a comprehensive NCD management course

actual.value: 117 chronic NCD patients have been enrolled.

target.value: 200 chronic NCD patients have been enrolled in and completed a comprehensive NCD management course At least 75% of chronic NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course have adopted and are applying healthier dietary and lifestyle changes for improved self-monitoring and daily management of their disease 40% of the most vulnerable NCD patients have received regular prescribed NCD medication support

actual.value: 203 chronic NCD patients (target: 200) (102 F; 83 M) were enrolled in the comprehensive NDC management course of which 197 completed the full year. Of these, 143 were Syrian Refugees (86 F; 57 M) and 60 Jordanian (34 F; 26 M). 86% of NCD patients enrolled in the NCD management course report that the program changed their nutritional behaviour and 89% reported experiencing benefits from the awareness sessions and topics throughout the programme.

title.narrative: Secondary health care services provided to 3,750 of patients annually

# of patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age and nationality, referred for SHC out-patient diagnostic and treatment services to Caritas partner SHC providers # of patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age, and nationality, referred for SHC in-patient diagnostic and treatment services (excluding deliveries) to Caritas partner SHC providers # of women and girls who have delivered in the presence of a skilled attendant under the programme

target.value: 3,120 patients referred to SHC out-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 570 patients referred to SHC in-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 60 women and girls who have delivered in the presence of a skilled attendant

2,490 patients referred to SHC out-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 285 patients referred to SHC in-patient diagnostic and treatment services annually 36 women and girls who have delivered in the presence of a skilled attendant

actual.value: 3,058 patients (target: 2,810) were referred to and supported with Secondary Health Care (outpatient and inpatient) services at Caritas partner hospitals, laboratories or from specialist consultants. Of these, 2,684 were referred for outpatient care (1,745 F; 936 M and 1,937 Syrian; 744 Jordanian) and 377 for inpatient care (192 F; 185 M and 267 Syrian; 110 Jordanian) of which 28 were deliveries (21 normal vaginal deliveries and 7 caesarean section deliveries).

title.narrative: Primary health care services provided to 6,000 unique patients annually

# of unique patients annually, disaggregated by gender, age and nationality, who have received essential primary health care services at Caritas clinics under the programme # of pregnant women and girls, who have accessed, and utilised maternal and neo-natal health care services provided by Caritas clinics

actual.value: 6,000 unique patients received PHC services (target: 6,000) including pre- and post-natal monitoring of 300 pregnant women, 6 of whom were <18 years. 89% of the pregnant women attended at least 7 of the 8 standard pre-and post-natal GP check-ups.
